transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um, hi. I just... I guess I've been having these nagging thoughts lately. Just worrying that I forgot something important. Like... maybe leaving my aunt's medicine out wrong, or... I teach, so, not setting up my classroom materials safely. I know I probably handled it fine, but... the doubt just keeps popping back into my head. So... that's why I'm here.
When these worrying thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly — like checking things over and over, counting, or trying to 'neutralize' the thought with another thought?

Um... yeah, I suppose. I just... before I leave the house or my classroom, I'll go back and look at the same things a few times. Like my aunt's pill organizer, or the stove... or my lesson plans. Or I'll just kind of... silently replay what I did in my head. 

I just do it until I feel calm enough to actually move on. It's... I mean, it makes me run late sometimes, but... yeah. I just check a few times.
How much time do these checking behaviors usually take, and do they ever interfere with your daily schedule or cause you a lot of distress?

Um... it's hard to say exactly how much time. Maybe... an extra twenty or thirty minutes in the mornings? 

I mean, I'm still getting everything done. I show up for work, I help my aunt. It's just... I guess my mornings take longer now. Sometimes I get to school feeling pretty rushed, like I'm already behind before the kids even get there. And... I don't know, things like getting my lesson plans ready or just trying to write in my journal at night... they just don't feel as relaxing or as smooth as they used to. But... I'm still managing, mostly.
When you check things like your aunt's pills or the stove, is it because you're afraid something bad might happen if you don't check them, or is it more just a habit that helps you feel ready?

Um... I don't know if it's a specific fear of something bad happening. Like I said earlier, it's really just... before I leave the house, or my room at school, I just feel like I have to go back over those things again. The pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans... or just replaying it all in my head. 

I just do it until I feel calm enough to actually walk away. If I don't, I just feel... unsettled. So I keep doing it until that feeling stops, so I can move on, even if it makes me late.
Do these thoughts about forgetting something or not doing something right feel intrusive and unwanted, or do they feel more like a normal part of your routine that you just want to double-check?

Um... they're definitely unwanted. I don't... I don't want to be thinking about them. 

It's just... these nagging thoughts keep popping up. Like, I'll think I left my aunt's medicine out wrong, or that I didn't set up the classroom safely. And... even when I know I probably handled it, the doubt just keeps coming back. That's... that's why I came in, really. I just want them to stop.
When you’re checking things like the stove or your aunt’s pills, do you feel like you’re trying to prevent something bad from happening, even if you know it might not make sense logically?

Um... I think I kind of mentioned this a minute ago, but... I don't really know if it's about preventing a specific bad thing. I know it doesn't always make sense. 

It's just... before I leave the house or my classroom, I just have to go back over those same things a few times. The pills, the stove, my lesson plans... or just silently replaying what I did in my head. I just keep doing it until I feel calm enough to actually move on... even when I know it's making me run late. That's really all it is.

Are there any other thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that you find disturbing or that you try to ignore or suppress, aside from concerns about forgetting something or not doing things correctly?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't think I have anything else like that. Just what we already talked about.

Have you ever felt driven to perform certain actions or rituals in a very specific way, not just to prevent something bad from happening, but because you feel like they absolutely must be done a certain way to feel right?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I just check the things I mentioned. There's no special way I have to do it or anything. Just... making sure it's done.

When you're feeling that unsettled feeling before you check things, do you ever try to manage it by doing something else in your mind or body—like silently repeating a word, counting, or focusing on a specific sensation—to feel more in control?

Um... no. Not really counting or repeating words. Like I said before, I just... I just replay what I did in my head. Like, mentally going back over everything I did before leaving the house or my classroom. I just do that, or check the things I mentioned, until I feel calm enough to leave. That's... that's really it.
Have you ever had any other types of recurring thoughts or urges that bother you, or felt like you needed to do other things in a certain way, even if you couldn't explain why?
No, I... I don't think so. I feel like I've already told you everything that bothers me. There really isn't anything else going on.

Do you ever feel like you have to arrange things in a certain way, make things symmetrical, or get something just right in your mind before you can move on, even if it's not about safety or forgetting something?

No... not at all. I don't really care if things are perfectly lined up or... symmetrical. I don't do any of that. Like I said, it's really just what we already talked about. I don't have any of these other things you're asking about.
Do you ever focus on a specific physical sensation—like how something feels when you touch it, or how your body feels—while you're checking things or trying to feel calm?
No... I don't really pay attention to how things feel like that. I just... I just check them. I'm not focusing on my body or anything. Just making sure it's done.

When you check those things, like the stove or your aunt’s pills, does it feel like you’re trying to prevent something bad from happening, or does it feel more like you’re trying to get a sense that things are ‘just right’ or complete before you move on?

I guess... I just do it until I feel calm. Like, before I leave the house or my classroom, I'll just go back over the same things a few times. The stove, the pill organizer... my lesson plans. Or I'll just silently replay what I did in my head. 

I don't know about it being "just right," I just... I need to feel calm enough to move on. Even if it makes me run late sometimes. I just need to feel settled before I can go.

Have you ever had any other concerns or rituals, even small ones, that you haven’t mentioned yet—like worrying about germs, needing to know or remember certain things perfectly, or feeling that something bad might happen to you or someone else if you don’t do something specific?

No... I don't have any of that. I don't worry about germs or anything. And I don't think something awful is going to happen to someone if I don't do something. It's really just... what I already said. I just check those few things, and that's it. There isn't really anything else.

When you check things like the stove or your aunt's pills, is it mainly because you feel like something bad could happen if you don't, or does it feel more like something inside just needs to be settled before you can move on, even if you can't explain why?
I... I think I just said that. It's not because I think something bad is going to happen. I just... like I said, I just need to feel settled. That's really all it is.
Have you ever had any other persistent thoughts or concerns that you try to manage by doing something specific, even if it's not something you've talked about yet?
No... I really don't. I feel like I'm repeating myself, but... no. There isn't anything else. Just the things we already talked about.
When you check things like the stove or your aunt's pills, is it mainly to stop worrying that something bad might happen, or is it more about needing to reduce that unsettled feeling inside?

I... didn't you just ask me that? Like I said, it's not about worrying that something bad will happen. It's just about that feeling. 

Before I leave the house, or my classroom, I just... I'll go back over the same things a few times. Checking the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans... or sometimes I just silently replay what I did in my head. I just do it until I feel calm enough to move on. Even if it makes me run late sometimes. That's... that's really all it is.
Have you ever had any other thoughts or worries that you try to manage by doing something specific, even if it's just a small thing or something you do quietly in your mind?
I... you just asked me that, too. No. I don't have anything else like that. Just the stuff we already went over. I don't really know what else to tell you.
